extracted.intended_audience: readers of an early-18th-century periodical interested in literature, theatre, and social manners (London literate public, critics, and men of letters)
extracted.subtask_description: A short periodical essay addressing literary criticism (poetry and theatre) and norms of social conversation in early-18th-century London; mixes critique, anecdote, and moral observation. Useful for guidance on what counts as good poetry, acceptable puppet-theatre, and proper conversational conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sublime poetic imagery (as exemplified in 'The Campaign')
rubrics_metrics.description: A great poem uses sublime images and similes (e.g., 'the simile of a ministering angel') that set forth both sedate and active courage amid tumult and horror.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such imagery should heighten the natural horrors by fresh, striking images; compliment relevant figures (here, the General and his Queen) while remaining 'familiar and heroic.' A successful poem can function both as poem and chronicle, preserving the memory of its subject beyond monuments and statues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance of the familiar and the heroic in poetic style
rubrics_metrics.description: The style should keep up 'the ordinary ideas of a march of an army' in a warm and great manner while being at once familiar and heroic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid alienating the reader with excessive grandeur; aim for diction that communicates heroic subject-matter in a way accessible to readers, so the work serves as both a chronicle and an exalted poem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Puppet drama is a legitimate (if minor) theatrical form
rubrics_metrics.description: Plays represented by puppets are permitted in universities and are 'not wholly thought unworthy the critic of learned heads.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat puppet-theatre as a form with its own decorum: its transitions (from mournful to merry, hanging to jigging) have a logic; performance features (single reciter, prompter, vocal machines) should be accounted for in criticism. Critics may lay down rules to adjust extravagant behaviour (e.g., Punchinello) and assess propriety toward audiences (especially regarding indecencies directed at ladies).

rubrics_metrics.name: Decorum and transition in low dramatic forms (tragi-comedy/punchinello)
rubrics_metrics.description: This sort of dramatic poetry has natural transitions—from mournful to merry, hanging of a lover to dancing on a rope, stalking of a ghost to a jig—that constitute its decorum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critics should recognise and evaluate the internal coherence of these transitions, the antiquity/chronology of the form, and whether its comic or ribald elements overstep acceptable bounds for the audience (e.g., indecencies toward women).

rubrics_metrics.name: Good conversation is founded on benevolence and mutual goodwill
rubrics_metrics.description: Conversation's essence is mutual goodwill and benevolence; learning, wit, gallantry, and good breeding are subordinate and valuable only insofar as they are subservient to benevolence and equality among company.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer companions who are 'natural' rather than merely 'acquired' in manners—those who speak from goodwill, avoid calumny, and do not seek superiority. The best companions show forbearance of bitterness and exemplify generous behaviour rather than ostentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not import social rank into conversation (practical rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: A person who brings his quality (social rank) with him into conversation is arriving to receive homage, not to meet friends; such a person 'should always pay the reckoning.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conversation should be among people 'as they are men,' not as distinguished by fortune. Social superiority in behaviour is a breach of conversational norms—practical remedy: those seeking deference ought to bear the cost (literal or figurative) of imposing their rank.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualities of an admirable companion
rubrics_metrics.description: An exemplary companion is good-natured, venerated for benevolence, not a braggart, and acts as an example rather than a check; such persons inspire natural, equal discourse among younger people.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value forbearance, absence of ostentation, and a disposition that takes off the necessity of caution in others. The companion's presence should reduce extremes of behaviour (neither 'grave nor gay above their years') and foster communicable temper rather than competition for superiority.
